Senses.Explanation: All things are consciousness-only is an inherited proposition that Chan records repeatedly put under pressure in face-to-face questioning. Yongming Yanshou presents it as a scriptural formula, but Huangbo Xiyun says the paired mind-only and consciousness-only wording was spoken against outside wrong views and refuses to make it a final resting place. Xitang Zhizang asks a purple-robed lecturer to state consciousness-only, then points to the door panel and asks what it is. In the Fayan case, Luohan Guichen invokes the same formula before asking whether a courtyard stone is inside or outside mind. Bie'an Xingtong retells Guichen’s test after rejecting the explicitly unnamed questioner’s conceptual explanation as ‘not yet’; Dahui Zonggao likewise describes Xiaonan as having mastered the formula before a separate encounter overturned that settled account. The entry therefore records both the proposition and its observable Chan deployment as material for testing. It does not adopt an outside systematic exposition as the definition of Zen.
